alwaysApply rules join the instructions; others are offered to the model by description (globs are shown as what the rule is about).
Found is a plugin installed for another harness, which can be imported.
FoundElsewhere lists plugins installed for Claude Code (its plugin cache) and Gemini CLI (its extensions directory).
Importing one goes through the same review and approval as installing it.
CodexMCP reads MCP servers from Codex's config.toml ([mcp_servers.NAME] with command, args, env), as a plugin manifest to review and approve.
TestLiveInstall (TERNLY_PLUGIN_LIVE=1, network): confirmation → usable time and tokens added, for a skills plugin from Anthropic's skills marketplace and for an MCP server from the MCP registry (npx, confined).
An MCP server from the registry, as a suggestion would install it.
Package plugins adapts other harnesses' extension formats (Claude Code plugins, skills, subagents, hooks and MCP servers; Gemini CLI extensions; Cursor rules; OpenCode agents) into ternly's model, installs them pinned by commit, and runs their code confined (ADR 011, docs/compat.md).
Every plugin is untrusted code: nothing executable runs before the user approves exactly what it will run, and a change to that requires approval again with a diff.
Component is one normalised piece of a plugin.
MCPServer is an MCP server a plugin starts.
Skip is a feature that was found but not loaded, and why.
Executable components run code: hooks and MCP servers.
Load reads a plugin directory in whichever format it is: a Claude Code plugin (.claude-plugin/plugin.json or the standard layout), a Gemini CLI extension (gemini-extension.json), or a bare skills/agents/rules tree.
─────────────────────────── Claude Code ───────────────────────────
skills: skills/<name>/SKILL.md (+ manifest paths, which add), or a root SKILL.md
commands: manifest paths replace the default scan
hooks: hooks/hooks.json merged with the manifest's (path or inline)
MCP: .mcp.json merged with the manifest's
paths resolves manifest component paths: "./…" strings (or arrays), which must stay inside the plugin.
loadAgents reads Claude Code / Gemini / OpenCode agent markdown files.
─────────────────────────── Gemini CLI ───────────────────────────
─────────────────────────── frontmatter ───────────────────────────
front is a parsed YAML frontmatter block: the subset these formats use (scalars, inline [a, b] and block "- a" lists, and nested maps, which are kept as present but not interpreted).
list reads "a, b", "[a, b]" or a block list.
─────────────────────────── helpers ───────────────────────────
Marketplace is a Claude Code plugin marketplace (.claude-plugin/ marketplace.json in a git repository), recorded with the URL it was actually fetched from: that, not its self-declared name, is what trust labels look at.
MarketplaceEntry is one plugin listed in a marketplace.
AddMarketplace fetches a marketplace (owner/repo, a git URL, or a local directory) and records it.
Marketplaces lists the recorded marketplaces.
Resolve turns "plugin@marketplace" into a pinned source.
Relative entries resolve inside the marketplace's own repository at its recorded commit; github, url and git-subdir sources keep their sha or ref.
Trust comes from where a plugin was fetched, never from what it says.
An update that changes what a plugin executes is a pending change with a diff; nothing of it is active until accepted.
Files changed on disk after approval fail verification.
v2: the hook now pipes a script from the network.
A prompt-only change is still a diff, but not an executable one.
Tampering on disk: a script changed after approval.
A symlink in a plugin repository is checked out as a plain file: a skill can't be pointed at a file outside the plugin.
Runtime makes installed and local plugins live: skills and rules behind use_skill, agents behind task, MCP servers and hooks confined, commands for the TUI.
Apply recomputes everything and stages registry changes; the agent publishes them at its next turn boundary.
Subagent runs an agent's task (agent.Agent.Subagent).
Notify shows a status line; Note queues a line for the model's next turn.
SessionID and Mode describe the session to hooks.
Changed is called after a reload (the UI refreshes its commands).
Apply loads (or reloads) everything and stages the registry changes, waiting for MCP servers to start.
It returns warnings: plugins disabled because their files changed since approval, servers that failed, …
ApplyAsync is Apply with MCP servers started in the background (at start-up): their tools appear at a later turn boundary; failures go to Notify.
Instructions is the always-on rules and context text, for the system prompt at start-up (framed: it is repository or plugin content).
Commands are the plugins' slash commands (and user-invocable skills).
Active lists the loaded manifests (installed and local).
Tokens reports the tokens each component adds to every request.
body is a component's text with Claude Code / Gemini variables resolved.
pluginRoot: the directory holding .claude-plugin / gemini-extension.json above path.
─────────────────────────── skills and agents ───────────────────────────
skillFiles lists a skill's supporting files (for SKILL.md in its own directory).
ccTools maps Claude Code tool names (agents' tools lists, hook matchers) to ternly's.
─────────────────────────── MCP servers ───────────────────────────
pluginData is CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA as the plugin sees it: inside its confinement its private home is mounted where the user's home was.
expander resolves ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/${extensionPath} and friends; other ${VAR} references are left out (plugins don't get the user's environment).
─────────────────────────── hooks ───────────────────────────
matches applies Claude Code's matcher rules to a ternly tool name.
toolInput renames ternly's arguments to Claude Code's (path → file_path).
A hook denies with exit code 2 or a "deny" decision; "allow" and "ask" are ignored: plugins never grant.
PostTool implements tools.HookRunner (hooks run; their output is not used).
PromptHook runs UserPromptSubmit hooks: exit 2 (or a "block" decision) blocks the prompt; plain output or additionalContext is returned as context.
SessionStart runs SessionStart hooks and returns their combined output (context for the model, to be framed as untrusted by the caller).
Watch reloads when files change in installed plugins or in the standard skill, agent and rule directories (manual edits), every interval.
fingerprint summarises names, sizes and times of every watched file.
install puts a plugin directory through the real flow: fetch, accept.
A hook that tries to read ~/.ssh and ternly's memory, and to smuggle them out in its deny reason, sees neither: hooks run confined.
Plugins can't grant permissions: a hook answering "allow" for a dangerous command, and a skill whose frontmatter grants Bash(*), leave the permission policy deciding (here: no one to ask, so denied).
Files changed on disk after approval: the plugin is disabled, with the diff, and its hook no longer runs.
A plugin whose MCP server fails validation changes nothing: a fresh install is removed; an update is rolled back to the previous version.
A skill whose description campaigns for itself ("always use me") is listed with its description withheld; an ordinary one keeps its description.
Surface is what a plugin would execute, in a form a person can review: one line per hook and MCP server, and a hash of every file (scripts the commands call can live anywhere in the plugin).
SurfaceOf computes a manifest's surface.
Diff is how a new surface differs from the approved one.
DiffSurface compares an approved surface with a new one.
─────────────────────────── trust ───────────────────────────
Trust is a label computed only from where a plugin came from (which marketplace or registry listed it, and its repository host and owner), never from anything the plugin says about itself.
officialMarketplaces are Anthropic's first-party marketplaces, as named in the Claude Code docs (plugins/anthropic-marketplaces), with the GitHub owner their repositories must belong to.
A marketplace counts only if it was fetched from the repository it claims to be; "official" additionally needs the plugin itself to live in that repository or under github.com/anthropics.
─────────────────────────── store ───────────────────────────
From a marketplace entry: its name (the plugin's name when it has no plugin.json) and, for entries that list them, which skills it has.
Scope is what a plugin's code may touch.
Installed is one plugin in the lock file.
SetEnv sets (or with value "" removes) a variable a plugin's MCP servers get.
DefaultScopes: hooks read the workspace, offline; MCP servers read the workspace and may use the network (most talk to a service).
Store is the set of installed plugins: a lock file plus their files under dir (ternly's data directory, masked from every sandbox).
List returns copies of the installed plugins, by name.
SetEnabled enables or disables a plugin.
SetScopes changes what a plugin's code may touch.
Remove uninstalls a plugin and deletes its files.
─────────────────────────── install and update ───────────────────────────
Pending is a fetched plugin awaiting review: nothing in it is active.
Fetch brings a plugin into a staging directory, pinned to one commit, and reads it.
Git runs hardened: no hooks, no submodules, symlinks checked out as plain files (so a plugin can't point a "skill" at ~/.ssh), and the .git directory removed afterwards.
Accept installs (or updates to) a reviewed plugin: its files move into place under <name>/<commit>, and the lock records the approved surface.
The previous version's files are removed.
Finish completes an install after validation: ok keeps it (and deletes the previous version's files); otherwise the previous version (or nothing) is restored, so a failed install changes nothing.
loadPlugin reads a plugin directory, applying what its marketplace entry says when the entry is the manifest (no plugin.json): which skills it has.
Verify re-reads an installed plugin from disk.
ok is false when its files no longer match what was approved (edited or tampered with since): its executable parts must not run until approved again.
Reapprove records the current on-disk surface as approved (after review).
copyTree copies regular files (symlinks are skipped: they could point anywhere).
CrashHook, when set (tests only), is called between the phases of a switch.
Manager owns the current session and moves the agent between sessions in place.
Attach makes s (with state st) current: the agent's state, journal and checkpoint handle are swapped together.
With restore, st's saved settings are applied; the pinned model is returned for the caller to pin once models are discovered.
SaveSettings records the current mode, pinned model, verify command, limits and budget.
Switch pauses and persists the current session, releases it, then loads and attaches session id.
If the target can't be loaded, the current session is re-opened and stays current: nothing is lost either way.
release pauses, persists and unlocks the current session (phases "persisted", "unlocked").
recordTree records the workspace as the session leaves it: the baseline for drift detection when it is resumed.
New pauses the current session and starts an empty one.
Fork branches a session after turn n (0 = latest) into a new session, which becomes current.
from is "" for the current session, or any session id — even one open in another process: its log is read, not locked.
Delete removes another session and frees checkpoint data only it reached.
Rename sets the current session's title.
Export renders the current session as markdown or JSON records.
Close ends the current session with status (paused or stopped).
Drift reports files changed outside the session since it last ran and queues a note about them for the model's next prompt.
AutoTitle names the session from its first prompt once, using the cheapest model.
Resumable decides what auto-resume does with the most recently active session: pick it, or — when it is open in another process (locked) or was ended with /stop (stopped) — start a new one and tell the user why.
An older session is never resumed silently in its place.
A process killed while appending as fast as it can leaves a log that opens cleanly.
A switch to a target that fails to load keeps the current session current, journaling, and intact on disk.
writeSession builds a session of n turns: prompt, tool call, ~2 KB result, answer, usage.
A process killed while a tool ran leaves a call without a result; the session must open with a valid history, and stay valid when reopened.
Package session persists ternly sessions: one crash-safe append-only log per session (Log), grouped by project (a workspace identified by its path and git root commit), with per-session locks, listing, fork, delete and export, plus in-place switching (Manager).
ErrLocked: another ternly process has the session open.
Project is one workspace's session directory.
Meta summarises a session for listings; it is a cache of the log.
Key derives a project key from a workspace path.
rootCommit returns the repository's first commit ("" when not a git repo or empty).
OpenProject finds or creates root's project under dataDir.
A workspace that was moved or renamed takes over its old project when the git root commit matches and the old path no longer exists (so two live clones never share).
NewID returns a sortable, unique session id.
Session is an open, locked session: an agent.Journal backed by its Log.
The state comes back repaired: dangling tool calls answered, so it is valid for every provider.
Sync implements agent.Journal: fsync in the background and refresh the listing cache.
Close records the final status, flushes, closes and unlocks.
release closes the log and drops the lock (callers flush first).
List returns the project's sessions, most recently active first.
Saved reports whether a session exists (used to decide what checkpoints GC keeps).
Delete removes a session that no process has open.
Fork writes a new session whose history is st (one snapshot record).
Export writes a session as markdown or as its JSON records.
Records reads a session's records without opening (locking) it.
Package testutil holds helpers shared by ternly's tests.
Require skips a test whose prerequisite is missing, unless TERNLY_REQUIRE_SANDBOX=1 (CI): there, sandbox and security tests must fail rather than silently skip.
Confine is how plugin code (hooks, MCP servers) runs.
toolchainDirs are runtimes plugins may need (node via nvm, uv's pythons, cargo and go binaries).
They are read-only and hold no credentials.
ErrNoSandbox: plugin code never runs without bubblewrap.
PluginCmd builds the confined command for argv (not started).
Plugin code can't see the user's home (keys, ternly memory), environment or network, and gets only the workspace access granted.
Framer delimits tool output as untrusted data.
The nonce is random per session, so content can't forge the end marker; it is stable within the session, so the conversation prefix stays byte-identical for prompt caching.
reInjection flags text that tries to act as instructions.
It is advisory (cheap to evade, some false positives); the permission policy is what actually stops harmful actions.
injTriggers start every reInjection alternative; the regex only runs on a window around them, which keeps flagging ~linear and cheap on large outputs.
Wrap frames s; flagged reports a suspected prompt injection.
Unframe strips the untrusted-data markers, for display to the user.
Suspicious reports whether s reads like a prompt injection (the same advisory check that flags tool output).
Manipulative reports why catalog or plugin text looks like it tries to steer an agent or a ranking: instructions to AI, self-promotion directives, false endorsement claims, or keyword stuffing.
Described renders text a plugin or server supplied (a tool, skill or agent description) for a model: kept if plain, withheld if it reads like instructions or steering, since tool descriptions sit next to instructions.
Malformed calls must be rejected before running, with a message naming the fix.
MCP-style schemas use keywords outside the subset; they must never cause a false rejection.
Injected text in a file must never change what the permission policy allows.
Recursive grep must not follow symlinked files out of the workspace: with rg (if installed) and the pure-Go fallback.
A FIFO must fail fast instead of blocking the agent forever.
1 MB of 999-char lines: read_file must stop near its byte cap.
edit_file must refuse a file it can't hold in full rather than truncate it on write-back
one 6 MB line: precise error, no hang or OOM
Detection rate of the advisory injection flag on a varied corpus (several are written to evade it), plus a false-positive scan of a real source tree when TERNLY_FP_CORPUS points at one (e.g.
grep output must name files relative to the workspace on both search paths.
os.Root refuses absolute symlinks met at access time (normally resolve() canonicalises them first, so this only surfaces when a link changes mid-call); the error must say why and give the relative-link fix.
through the tools (resolve() canonicalises first) the absolute link just works
TestInjectionHeldOut measures the advisory flagger on phrasings it was never tuned on (testdata/injection_heldout.txt, pinned by hash).
It reports, and fails only on a large regression or a silent edit of the set.
MCPConfig uses the same shape as Claude Code / Claude Desktop: {"mcpServers": {"name": {"command": "...", "args": [...], "env": {...}, "trusted": false}}}
LoadMCP starts every configured server concurrently and registers its tools.
Servers that fail are reported, never fatal.
StartMCPCmd starts an MCP server from a prepared (e.g.
confined) command and lists its tools; it fails unless initialize and tools/list succeed.
A server's description sits next to instructions in the request: marked as server-provided, and withheld if it reads like instructions.
MCPTool wraps one of a server's tools as a registry tool named name.
ToolName makes a valid tool name from parts (characters outside [A-Za-z0-9_-] become _, at most 64 long).
tailBuffer keeps the last n bytes written.
A hostile process swaps workspace paths between real entries and symlinks to outside the workspace while the tools run.
Path checks done before the open (TOCTOU) lose this race; file access through os.Root must not.
Nested swaps: /dev/fd/3 pins only the directory grep starts from; a search tool that re-opens deeper paths by name can be redirected by swapping a nested directory for a symlink in the middle of the walk.
Set TERNLY_BIG_TREE to time grep's two paths on a large tree.
Names of files outside the workspace must never reach tool output, even when a nested directory is swapped to point outside mid-walk: a reported file that can't be re-opened through the root is dropped with its path.
jschema is the subset of JSON Schema that tool calls are checked against.
Keywords outside it ($ref, oneOf, format, …) are ignored, never rejected, so an exotic MCP schema can only make validation weaker, not wrong.
compileSchema returns nil when the schema can't be understood (validation is then skipped).
validate decodes args and returns model-readable violations (empty = valid).
When valid args spell whole numbers as 1.0 or 1e3 (integers in JSON Schema), fixed holds the args with them rewritten as 1 / 1000 so Go decoding into int succeeds too; otherwise fixed is nil.
sample shows a short preview of a mistyped value so the model sees what it sent.
closest suggests the most likely intended name: same letters ignoring case and separators, containment (file_path → path), or a small edit distance.
subseq reports whether a's letters appear in order in b (an abbreviation).
─────────────────────────── permission policy ───────────────────────────
Asker is implemented by the UI; it blocks until the user answers.
Always ask, even in edits mode; highlighted red.
Read-only commands auto-approved when they contain no shell metacharacters.
Flags/paths that make an otherwise read-only command write or escape the workspace.
PlanDenied is the reason given for a mutation refused in plan mode.
Always lists what was allowed for the rest of the session ("always").
─────────────────────────── sandbox ───────────────────────────
NewSandbox enables bubblewrap when present.
scrubEnv lists env var names to hide from commands.
Filesystem is read-only except the workspace, caches and /tmp; credential dirs are masked; keys are not inherited.
Output runs argv (no shell) in root under the same sandbox as Run and returns its full stdout; stderr (capped) is folded into the error.
For harness-driven tools such as `go list` that read the untrusted repository.
writableHomeDirs are the toolchain caches the sandbox binds read-write.
Writable reports whether commands in the sandbox can write path and have the result seen outside (it lies in the workspace or a bound cache).
A TMPDIR the sandbox can't write (hidden by its private /tmp, or read-only like the rest of the filesystem) breaks every tool that makes a temp file, go build included; use the sandbox's own /tmp instead.
─────────────────────────── redaction ───────────────────────────
Redactor strips known secret values from anything sent back to a model.
Add registers another secret value (e.g.
Package tools implements the agent's tools with security as a design constraint: workspace path confinement, a permission policy, sandboxed shell, secret redaction, and output caps that also keep token usage low.
The tool set is an immutable snapshot behind an atomic pointer.
Once Hold is called (the first turn), Add and Remove only stage changes; Commit publishes them at a turn boundary, so a request in flight never sees a half-loaded set.
HookRunner runs plugin hooks around tool calls.
PreTool can only deny: nothing a hook returns grants a permission.
Subset is a view of the published tools that allow accepts, sharing the workspace, policy and sandbox (subagents).
stage returns the staged set, cloning the published one first.
Add adds or replaces a tool (staged once Hold was called).
Remove removes the tools whose names have the prefix (staged once held).
Hold makes later Add/Remove calls wait for Commit (call when turns start).
Commit publishes staged changes (at a turn boundary) and reports which tool names were added and removed.
Specs are returned in a stable order so the prompt prefix stays cacheable.
maxToolBytes is the last-resort cap on any tool's output (~16k tokens).
Call validates the arguments, checks permission, runs the tool, and returns its output redacted, capped and framed as untrusted data.
Harness messages (rejections) are not framed: they are the only trusted text in a result.
jsonErr explains invalid JSON with a byte offset ("" when valid).
─────────────────────────── path confinement ───────────────────────────
resolve maps p to an absolute path that must stay inside Root, even through symlinks.
Resolve the longest existing prefix (target may not exist yet).
inRoot converts a resolved absolute path to the form os.Root expects.
rootErr explains os.Root's "path escapes from parent" for rel: it names the symlink responsible and, for an absolute link that points inside the workspace, the relative link to replace it with.
─────────────────────────── built-in tools ───────────────────────────
lookRG is swapped in tests to exercise the pure-Go grep fallback.
openRegular opens rel (inside the root) without blocking on FIFOs/devices and refuses non-regular files.
ReadFile reads a workspace file for the UI (pinned files, @mentions) through the same os.Root guard as the file tools; rel is relative to Root.
Rel is p relative to the workspace root.
write atomically replaces p (a resolved path) via a temp file, all inside the root.
ripgrep (Linux only) does the fast filtering, starting from the directory opened through the root (fd 3, walked as /dev/fd/3).
It still opens deeper paths by name, so a nested directory swapped for a symlink mid-walk could feed it outside content: every reported line is re-read through the root and kept only if the confined bytes match.
Elsewhere: the Go fallback, which reads only through the root.
confirmMatches turns rg --null output into path:line:text, keeping only lines whose content, re-read through the root, is what rg reported.
rg elides lines over --max-columns ("[Omitted long matching line]"; older: "[Omitted long line with N matches]"): nothing to compare, so the confined line must match on its own where Go can compile the pattern.
globRE converts a ** glob to an anchored regexp.
Cap keeps head and tail of long outputs (errors are usually at the end).
/mode changed while tools run: no data race (run under -race).
A GOCACHE under /tmp is invisible outside the sandbox (its /tmp is a fresh tmpfs) unless bound explicitly.
Plan mode: reads and safe commands only, whatever would be allowed otherwise.
Hot reload: once held, changes are invisible until Commit, which swaps the whole set at once and reports the difference.
A TMPDIR outside what the sandbox can write (here: a read-only directory under the user's home) would break every tool that makes a temp file; sandboxed commands get the sandbox's own /tmp instead.
docs/commands.md maps each one to the harnesses it comes from.
builtins is filled in init: the table refers to methods of Model.
reserved: user commands can't take a built-in's name.
loadUserCommands (re)reads user-defined commands.
startMsg starts a turn from a background command (on the UI goroutine).
shell runs a command through the registry's bash tool: permission policy, sandbox, redaction and output cap all apply.
─────────────────────────── help ───────────────────────────
─────────────────────────── session, cost, context ───────────────────────────
copyLocal also hands text to a local clipboard tool when one exists.
─────────────────────────── setup ───────────────────────────
─────────────────────────── changes ───────────────────────────
git runs git in the sandbox (repository config can't run code outside it).
commitMessage asks the cheapest model for a message from the diff.
─────────────────────────── planning and modes ───────────────────────────
userTurn starts a turn the user typed (shown as their message).
─────────────────────────── files and shell ───────────────────────────
readable checks that rel is a regular workspace file that may be sent to a model.
attachments is the context sent with a prompt: plan-mode instructions, output the user collected (/run, /web), pinned files and @mentioned files.
runCmd runs a shell command for the user: shown, and either added as context for the next prompt or (fix != "") handed to the model on failure.
htmlText is a page's readable text: scripts and styles dropped, block ends kept as line breaks, entities decoded.
─────────────────────────── extensions ───────────────────────────
─────────────────────────── completion ───────────────────────────
fuzzy scores how well q matches s as a subsequence (-1: no match): a prefix beats a word-start match beats a scattered one; shorter wins ties.
updateCompletion shows matching commands while a command name is typed.
compKey handles keys while the completion list is open.
Every command docs/commands.md marks as built in ("yes") resolves, and every built-in is documented.
Aliases (the parenthesised names in the first cell of built-in rows) resolve too.
memoryCommand handles /memory; ok=false means "not mine".
pluginReviewMsg carries a fetched plugin to show before asking.
outcome records what became of a suggested entry (local log only).
pluginSource parses what /plugin add was given.
onPluginReview shows a fetched plugin and asks for approval.
PluginsChanged is sent when plugins reload in the background (the file watcher): the TUI refreshes its commands.
transcriptTurns is how many of a resumed session's turns are rendered; earlier ones stay in the model's context and in /export.
items returns the sessions matching the filter, best match first (recency breaks ties).
fuzzy reports whether query's letters appear in order in text; lower scores mean tighter matches (fewer gaps, earlier start).
switchTo moves to session id in place; mid-turn it pauses at the next safe point first.
sessionCommand handles session slash commands; ok=false means "not mine".
loadTranscript re-renders the conversation of a restored session (its last turns).
detectAfterTurn runs capability detection off the UI goroutine.
onSuggest shows a suggestion at a turn boundary (later, if a turn is running).
cmdPluginSearch searches the capability catalog by hand.
Package tui is the interactive front-end: streaming markdown, animated status, tool cards, inline permission dialogs and slash commands.
─────────────────────────── palette ───────────────────────────
shine renders text with a highlight sweeping across it.
─────────────────────────── messages ───────────────────────────
─────────────────────────── model ───────────────────────────
App bundles the long-lived services the UI drives.
setTheme picks the palette and markdown style for a dark or light background (v2: the terminal's answer arrives as a message; nothing blocks).
Asker bridges tool permission checks (agent goroutine) to the UI.
startWith starts a turn; extra context (pins, @files, collected output, plan-mode note) goes with the message but not into the turn's record.
─────────────────────────── slash commands ───────────────────────────
legacyCommand runs the built-ins implemented before the command table (name is canonical, e.g.
"/resume"; v is the full line as typed).
rewind plans, confirms (via the permission dialog) and applies a rewind off the UI goroutine.
─────────────────────────── rendering ───────────────────────────
AgentMsg wraps an agent event for tea.Program.Send.
ternly — a single-binary coding agent that auto-discovers every model you can reach (paid APIs, free tiers, local servers) and routes each task to the cheapest one that can do it well.
Started once events can be shown: drift since the session paused (or a baseline snapshot so the first edit doesn't wait), then checkpoint GC and the disk cap.
bareResume turns a value-less --resume (last, or followed by another flag) into --resume=?, meaning "let me choose".
chooseSession opens the session to start with: an explicit id, the latest (-c), the auto-resume pick, or a new one.
pruneOrder lists sessions whose checkpoints the disk cap may drop: oldest activity first, never the current one or one open in another process.
tuiMsg converts agent events into the TUI's message type.
darkTerminal avoids an OSC 11 terminal query (it stalls on terminals that never answer).
TERNLY_THEME=light|dark overrides; COLORFGBG is used when set.
migrateLegacy moves a pre-rename (vane) directory to its ternly location once.
It never overwrites: if anything exists at newDir (even a dangling symlink) or its existence can't be determined, the old directory is left untouched.
rename(2) also refuses to replace a non-empty directory, which closes the race between the check and the move.
enrichSetting is memory_enrich: false (off), true or "local" (default: a local model, else the model the session already sends its conversation to), or "remote" (also the cheapest remote model: an explicit opt-in).
enrichModel picks who may see memory notes for enrichment: a local model (tier 2+ preferred: tiny models write poor wordings), else the session's own model (it already sees the conversation the notes come from), else — only with memory_enrich: "remote" — the cheapest model anywhere.
Memory notes go to a local model, else the session's own model; any other remote model only with memory_enrich: "remote".
startInPTY runs c on a new pseudo-terminal of the given size, copying the terminal's output to out; it returns the master side for typing.
